transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for grades 6 through 8, and I've asked each of you here because I need your input before I can sign off on the plan. The draft currently calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear any concerns or recommendations each of you has regarding these elements. Let's start with you — what do we need to consider from your area of expertise?

transcript.text: I need to flag a staffing concern. I received the finalized roster from the activities office yesterday, and it contains 18 student tutors. Our school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. That means we need at least three adult supervisors, not two. The draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two supervisors, so this needs to be updated before approval.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern about the student-selected tutor pairings. I completed a student-support review this week, and it revealed two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students who are seeking tutoring. For everyone's safety and to comply with those restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be student-selected. Instead, I will need to assign and monitor all pairings myself, based on the confidential information in my counseling files. The draft plan's approach of letting students choose their own partners would risk violating those no-contact orders.
